primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Left atrial myxoma with IL-6-mediated constitutional syndrome
mechanism: Atrial myxomas are benign primary cardiac tumors that most often arise from the left atrium near the interatrial septum/fossa ovalis. Their mobility can cause intermittent mitral inflow obstruction and systemic embolization. Tumor-cell secretion of interleukin-6 drives many constitutional manifestations and acute-phase responses.
vignette: A 46-year-old woman has 4 months of fatigue, low-grade fevers, weight loss, and intermittent exertional dyspnea that is worse when she lies in certain positions. Examination reveals a low-pitched diastolic sound after S2 that varies with body position. Erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein are elevated. Echocardiography shows a pedunculated mass attached to the interatrial septum near the fossa ovalis that intermittently prolapses through the mitral valve.
lead: Which mediator is most likely responsible for this patient’s constitutional symptoms and elevated acute-phase reactants?
distractors: Histamine released from tumor-associated mast cells
Erythropoietin secreted ectopically by the tumor
Parathyroid hormone-related peptide secreted by the tumor
Serotonin released from neuroendocrine granules within the tumor
distractor_notes: Histamine can mediate flushing, pruritus, and anaphylactoid symptoms, but it is not the characteristic cytokine responsible for the constitutional and acute-phase syndrome of atrial myxoma.
Ectopic erythropoietin causes erythrocytosis in selected tumors such as renal cell carcinoma and hepatocellular carcinoma; it does not explain the inflammatory syndrome of atrial myxoma.
PTH-related peptide causes humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy, not the typical fever, weight loss, elevated ESR, and CRP associated with cardiac myxoma.

Serotonin secretion is characteristic of carcinoid tumors and can cause flushing, diarrhea, and right-sided valvular fibrosis; atrial myxoma does not produce its constitutional syndrome through serotonin.
key_expl: The pedunculated left atrial mass attached near the fossa ovalis, positional obstructive symptoms, and variable diastolic 'tumor plop' identify an atrial myxoma. Myxoma cells can actively secrete IL-6. Circulating IL-6 stimulates hepatic acute-phase protein production and contributes to fever, malaise, weight loss, arthralgias, and elevated inflammatory markers. IL-6 concentrations and constitutional findings commonly fall after complete tumor resection.
objective: Recognize IL-6 secretion by atrial myxoma cells as the basis of the constitutional and acute-phase syndrome accompanying this otherwise histologically benign cardiac tumor.

sources.title: The role of interleukin-6 in cases of cardiac myxoma
sources.support: Prospective observations linked elevated IL-6 in atrial myxoma with constitutional and immunologic abnormalities and documented normalization of IL-6 and clinical manifestations after resection.
